MUQATIL:16:60-61/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:60-61/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:60-61/r2.claim: If God immediately punished Meccan unbelievers for disbelief, drought would kill every creature; instead he delays their punishment to the appointed time recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

MUQATIL:16:60-61/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:16:60-61/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:16:60-61/r3.claim: When the time of worldly punishment comes, it cannot be delayed or advanced.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70#2/r1.claim: At the appointed time, people cannot delay or advance the punishment even by an hour.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70/r3.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70/r3.claim: If God punished people for their wrongdoing immediately, withholding rain would destroy the animals on earth.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70/r4.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70/r4.claim: God delays the polytheists' punishment until the appointed Hour; this community's total destruction is deferred until the first trumpet blast.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p70/r5.claim: When their appointed punishment arrives, they can neither delay it by an hour nor bring it forward.

TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r1.claim: If God punished humanity immediately for its sins, no creature on earth would remain; in mercy He delays the wrongdoers to their appointed time, which cannot be advanced or postponed once it arrives.

TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r2.speaker: أبو الأحوص
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r2.claim: Abu al-Ahwas says a dung beetle nearly suffered punishment because of human sins, citing this verse.

TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra rejects the claim that an oppressor harms only himself: injustice can leave a bustard starving to death in its nest.

TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r4.claim: Ibn Masud says Adam’s sin killed the dung beetle; another wording says it nearly perished in its burrow.

TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r5.speaker: الزهري
TAB-FULL:v14p259#2/r5.claim: Al-Zuhri says the appointed time cannot be delayed once present, while before it God may delay or advance what He wills.

ZAJJAJ:v3p206/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p206/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p206/r3.claim: ʿAlayhā means ‘on the earth’; earth is implicit because animals live on it.

THALABI:v6p24#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p24#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p24#2/r1.claim: If God immediately punished people for their wrongs, no creature would remain on earth; instead He delays them to a fixed term, and no one can advance or postpone death by an hour.

THALABI:v6p24#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p24#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p24#2/r2.claim: عليها refers elliptically to the earth's surface, and the fixed term is the end of people's lifespans.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r1.claim: If God punished people in this life for their wrongdoing, He would destroy them in retribution, though He generally grants them respite.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r2.claim: ما ترك عليها من دابة means He would annihilate them with a wholesale punishment for their wrongdoing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r3.claim: أجل مسمى may mean the Day of Resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r4.claim: Alternatively, the appointed term may be a punishment advanced in this life.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r5.claim: The destruction of wrongdoers can be retribution while believing victims receive compensating reward in the afterlife.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, the phrase about leaving no creature can be restricted to unjust people.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p195#2/r7.claim: Alternatively, had God destroyed disbelieving ancestors, their descendants, including future believers, would never have been born.

QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r4.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r4.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r4.claim: Those marked by association face immediate punishment and accumulated anxieties.

QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r5.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r5.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r5.claim: If God punished people immediately for their wrongdoing, destruction would overtake them; prior decree instead grants delay until they meet their deeds’ consequences.

QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r6.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r6.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r6.claim: Ease deceives them into expecting escape, makes their bad traits appear good, and ends in regret with no prayer heard or mercy shown.

QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p161/r7.claim: The verse consoles Muhammad by recalling that earlier nations also strayed as his people did, while God remained fully able to deal with them.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r1.claim: In Ata's transmission, people means the polytheists and their wrongdoing means fabricating lies about God; the phrase about leaving no creature means no fabricator would remain.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r10.claim: Other commentators take the appointed term as the end of each lifespan, which the author considers closer because the polytheists are punished when their lives end.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r11.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r11.claim: The phrase that people neither delay nor advance an hour was explained earlier in the commentary on al-Aʿraf.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r2.claim: On that reading, God would immediately punish the fabricators and clear the earth of them; the unintroduced pronoun in عليها refers to earth, clear from the mention of creatures living on it.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r3.claim: With Ibn Abbas's interpretation, creature is restricted to a fabricator, whereas most other commentators understand all terrestrial creatures.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r4.speaker: السدي عن أصحابه
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r4.claim: They interpret the verse as drought withholding rain until every creature on earth perishes.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r5.claim: He says human sin nearly caused even the dung beetle in its hole to perish.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r6.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r6.claim: He says this kind of destruction already occurred in Noah's time.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r7.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r7.claim: He says rain is withheld so that everything would perish, explaining how the sins of the polytheists could endanger terrestrial creatures.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r8.speaker: أهل المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r8.claim: They explain that killing the fathers for disbelief would leave no children, emptying the earth; God delays punishment to an appointed term so people may reproduce.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r9.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p98/r9.claim: He identifies the appointed term as the Resurrection.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:60-61/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:60-61/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:60-61/r2.claim: The wrongdoing means polytheists' fabrication about God; were they punished immediately, no polytheist would remain alive anywhere.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:60-61/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:60-61/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:16:60-61/r3.claim: God delays punishment until an appointed lifespan expires.

JISHUMI:v6p4057/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4057/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4057/r10.claim: The pronoun in عليها refers to the unstated earth; Arabic commonly omits such an obvious referent, including when speaking of what is on a city or its two lava fields.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26#2/r1.claim: God gives people respite until their appointed term, the end of their lifespans; when it arrives, it cannot be advanced or delayed.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r1.claim: If God punished people at once for disbelief and disobedience, no creature would remain on earth; the pronoun refers implicitly to earth.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r2.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r2.claim: He says God did this in Noah's time, destroying all on earth except those aboard Noah's ark.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r3.claim: He rebuked a man who said injustice harms only the wrongdoer, saying even a partridge dies in its nest through a wrongdoer's injustice.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r4.claim: He says even a dung beetle is punished in its burrow for the sin of Adam's descendant.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p26/r5.claim: Another interpretation is that punishing the wrongdoers' ancestors would cut off their descendants, leaving nobody on earth.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p402#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p402#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p402#2/r6.claim: Yuʾākhidh is a reciprocal form of أخذ; the form can be understood as taking in response to sin or harm, with either of two verbal patterns.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p402#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p402#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p402#2/r7.claim: The pronoun عليها refers to the earth, though earth has not been named, because it is familiar and can be indicated without prior mention, as in the poem about the sun.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p402#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p402#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p402#2/r8.claim: The مِن in مِن دابة covers every kind of creature; the passage begins to explain that immediate punishment for deserved sin would leave no creature alive.

TABRISI:16:61-65/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61-65/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:61-65/r1.claim: A question asks why animals without guilt would suffer if wrongdoers deserve punishment. The answer is that their suffering is a lesson and trial, with compensation, like illness affecting saints and those not morally responsible.

TABRISI:16:61-65/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61-65/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:16:61-65/r2.claim: Alternatively, if the fathers perished through disbelief, their children would never exist.

TABRISI:16:61-65/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61-65/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:16:61-65/r3.claim: Alternatively, animals were created for morally responsible people, so there would be no purpose in their continuing after those people perished.

TABRISI:16:61-65/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61-65/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:61-65/r4.claim: The statement that people cannot delay or advance their appointed time was explained earlier.

TABRISI:16:61/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:61/r10.claim: Arabic commonly omits an understood place, as in ‘between its two lava fields’ for Medina and ‘it became cold’ for the morning.

TABRISI:16:61/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:61/r11.claim: The appointed term is Judgment Day, or a time God knows it is no longer beneficial to keep them alive because they will not believe and no believer will descend from them; postponement nevertheless allows repentance or serves a benefit.

TABRISI:16:61/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61/r12.speaker: أبو هاشم
TABRISI:16:61/r12.claim: On whether someone known never to believe may be spared, Abū Hāshim and al-Murtaḍā say continued life is permissible but not obligatory, since moral responsibility itself is a grace.

TABRISI:16:61/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61/r13.speaker: المرتضى
TABRISI:16:61/r13.claim: On whether someone known never to believe may be spared, Abū Hāshim and al-Murtaḍā say continued life is permissible but not obligatory, since moral responsibility itself is a grace.

TABRISI:16:61/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61/r14.speaker: البلخي
TABRISI:16:61/r14.claim: Al-Balkhī and Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī require continued life, but differ: al-Jubbāʾī calls its absence harmful, while al-Balkhī calls preservation the most beneficial choice; al-Mufīd agrees with al-Balkhī.

TABRISI:16:61/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61/r15.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:16:61/r15.claim: Al-Balkhī and Abū ʿAlī al-Jubbāʾī require continued life, but differ: al-Jubbāʾī calls its absence harmful, while al-Balkhī calls preservation the most beneficial choice; al-Mufīd agrees with al-Balkhī.

TABRISI:16:61/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61/r16.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:16:61/r16.claim: Alternatively, if God punished them, He would withhold rain until every animal perished.

TABRISI:16:61/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61/r17.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:16:61/r17.claim: Alternatively, if God punished them, He would withhold rain until every animal perished.

TABRISI:16:61/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:16:61/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:16:61/r9.claim: If God immediately punished all people for their wrongdoing, no creature on the earth who deserved punishment would remain; ‘on it’ refers implicitly to the earth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r1.claim: Their wrongdoing means their shirk and sins; if each were punished as it occurred, no creature would remain on earth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r2.claim: “On its back” refers to the earth, which is implied because living creatures are on it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masud says “creature” includes everything that moves on earth.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r4.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r4.claim: Qatada says this universal destruction occurred in Noah's time; al-Suddi and Muqatil explain it as drought killing all creatures by withholding rain.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r5.speaker: ابن جريج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r5.claim: Ibn Jurayj says “creature” means people specifically.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r6.speaker: ابن السائب والزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r6.claim: Ibn al-Sa'ib says the term means humans and jinn; al-Zajjaj chooses this view.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v4p459#2/r7.claim: The appointed term is the end of their lifespans; the remainder was explained under another verse.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r1.claim: The conditional is taken to show God did not seize people for their wrongdoing; since many creatures remain, the text is used to reject harm authorized as punishment for earlier crimes.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r2.claim: Harm imposed without a prior offense is also rejected by consensus, so the verse establishes a general presumption against harms; specific text can make an exception, otherwise harms are forbidden.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r3.claim: He supports the prohibition with verses against corruption, hardship, and difficulty, plus reports that there is no harming or reciprocal harm and that whoever harms a Muslim is cursed.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r4.speaker: ومنهم من قال
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r4.claim: Some extend the rule to say everything a person wants must be granted and everything disliked must be forbidden because denying or imposing it is harm.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p47#2/r5.claim: On that expansive view, analogy is redundant when it agrees with the rule and invalid when it conflicts with the text.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r1.claim: After recounting the people's grave disbelief and ugly speech, God explains that He delays these disbelievers rather than hastening punishment, showing grace, mercy, and generosity.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r2.speaker: الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r2.claim: Critics of prophetic impeccability argue that the verse attributes wrongdoing to all people, and prophets are people, so prophets must sin.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r3.speaker: الطاعنون في عصمة الأنبياء
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r3.claim: They also argue that if prophets were exempt from wrongdoing, destroying every wrongdoer would not entail leaving no creature on earth; the verse therefore makes everyone, including prophets, sinners.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r4.claim: Q 35:32 divides God's chosen servants into wrongdoers, moderate people, and those foremost in good works; if the latter groups were also wrongdoers, the division would collapse.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r5.claim: Therefore the people in this verse can mean either all sinners deserving punishment or the particular polytheists, including those who attributed daughters to God, so the critics' inference fails.

RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r6.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v20p47/r6.claim: Some use this verse to argue that harm is presumptively forbidden, since permitted harm would have to be either retribution for a prior offense or imposed without such an offense.

RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r1.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r1.claim: The Mu'tazilites argue wrongdoing is the people's act, not God's, because the verse assigns it to them; if God created it, punishing them would be injustice by God.

RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r2.speaker: المعتزلة
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r2.claim: They also say the verse's باء marks causation, making human acts effective causes of reward and punishment, as in Q 8:13.

RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r3.claim: The apparent claim that human wrongdoing would destroy every animal raises the problem that animals committed no sin.

RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r4.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r4.claim: Al-Jubba'i says immediate punishment for disbelief and sin would eliminate human descendants, since every person has an ancestor deserving punishment; animals would disappear too because they serve human interests.

RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r5.claim: Another answer says a destruction can punish wrongdoers while testing other people and animals, as occurred in Noah's time.

RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p48/r6.claim: A third answer says seizure would stop rainfall and plants, leaving no creature; Abu Hurayra reports a bustard dying in its nest from an oppressor's wrong, and Ibn Mas'ud says a dung beetle nearly perishes in its hole through Adam's children's sin.

RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r1.claim: An alternative is that dābbah means a disbeliever rather than every creature, supported by the description of some people as cattle or even further astray in Q 7:179.

RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r2.claim: The feminine pronoun in عليها refers to earth, though earth was not named; mentioning a creature implies the surface it crawls on, and Arabic often uses this idiom without naming earth.

RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r3.claim: The delay to a specified term allows people to reproduce.

RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r4.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r4.claim: One interpretation, transmitted by Ata from Ibn Abbas, takes the specified term to be the Day of Resurrection, when most punishment arrives.

RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v20p49/r5.claim: Another interpretation takes the term as the end of a lifespan: polytheists receive punishment when their lives end and they leave this world.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r1.claim: The appointed term is the limit of a person's life; when it comes there is no delay or advance.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r2.claim: Although collective destruction includes believers who are not unjust, the unjust die as punishment while believers receive compensation through the afterlife reward.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r3.speaker: ابن عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r3.claim: In Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim, ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet saying that if punishment strikes a people, those present are affected and then resurrected according to their intentions.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r4.speaker: أم سلمة
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r4.claim: When Umm Salama asks about an army swallowed in the desert while pursuing a refuge seeker at the Kaʿba, the Prophet says even the reluctant are swallowed with them but resurrected according to intention.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r5.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says he treated this issue at length in al-Tadhkira and refers readers to earlier discussions in al-Māʾida and the end of al-Anʿām.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61#2/r6.claim: An alternative interpretation takes the appointed term as the Day of Resurrection.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r1.claim: Taking people to account for their wrongdoing means punishing them immediately for disbelief and fabrication.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r2.claim: The phrase mā taraka ʿalayhā refers to the earth, though earth is unstated; the mention of creatures implies it because creatures walk on earth.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r3.claim: One interpretation restricts the creatures to unbelievers; another says destroying sinful parents would mean their descendants never existed.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan takes the wording universally: God would leave no creature on earth, prophet or otherwise, if He seized all people for what they earned.

QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود
QURTUBI-FULL:16:61/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says punishment for sinners would reach all creation, even beetles in their holes, stop rain and plants, and kill animals; God instead acts with pardon and grace, as in 42:30.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r2.claim: Wrongdoing here means disbelief and disobedience; the unmentioned earth is understood from people and creatures.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r3.claim: If people were punished immediately, not one creature would remain on earth due to their wrongdoing.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r4.claim: Ibn Masud reports that a dung beetle in its hole nearly perishes because of a human sin; another wording says because of an unjust creature.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r5.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r5.claim: If the unbelieving parents were destroyed, their children would not be born.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r6.claim: The appointed term may be their lifespans or their punishment, with respite allowing them to reproduce.

BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:16:60-61/r7.claim: Universal wording about people does not call every person, including prophets, sinful; a trait common to most may be ascribed to all.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r1.claim: Wrongdoing means disbelief and sins; if God punished people immediately, not one creature would remain on earth.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r2.claim: Abu Hurayra says even the bustard dies in its nest because of the wrongdoer's injustice.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the dung beetle nearly perishes in its hole because of a descendant of Adam's sin.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās interprets every creature as every moving polytheist.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p260#4/r5.claim: The appointed term may be each person's lifespan, a time set by wisdom, or the Resurrection; when it arrives, no delay or advancement is possible.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p549/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p549/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p549/r4.claim: After recounting their grave unbelief and attributing offspring to God, the verse says He delays punishment rather than hastening it, displaying grace and mercy.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p549/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p549/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p549/r5.claim: يؤاخذ is the form III imperfect of أخذ, apparently with the simple meaning of taking or seizing; Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains reciprocal taking as punishment for sin or injury.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p549/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p549/r6.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p549/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains mutual taking as God requiting sin or people answering one another's harm with punishment and recompense.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r1.claim: The implicit antecedent of عليها is earth, inferred from من دابة because creatures move on land; the author compares this ellipsis to a verse where the location of dust-raising is likewise supplied from context.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r2.claim: من دابة apparently includes every creature on earth, so the righteous would perish with the wicked; Ibn Masʿūd says even beetles in their holes would die.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r3.claim: Qatāda says God enacted this destruction in Noah's time; al-Suddī and Muqātil say drought would kill every creature.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r4.claim: Abū Hurayra rebuts the claim that an unjust person harms only himself: even a bird in its nest may die through the oppressor's wrongdoing.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r5.speaker: ابن السائب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v6p550/r5.claim: Ibn al-Sāʾib, a view chosen by al-Zajjāj, restricts the creatures to humans and jinn; Ibn Jurayj says humans only, while another group including Ibn ʿAbbās says only an unbelieving creature.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r1.claim: God bears patiently with His creatures despite their wrongdoing; if He punished them for their deeds, He would destroy every creature on earth along with humanity.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r2.claim: God delays punishment until an appointed term rather than hastening it, since immediate punishment would leave no one alive.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r3.speaker: أبو الأحوص
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Ahwas says a dung beetle nearly suffers punishment for human sins; a parallel report from Abdullah says one nearly dies in its burrow because of human wrongdoing.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r4.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra rebukes a man who said injustice harms only its perpetrator, saying even a bustard may die emaciated in its nest because of a tyrant's injustice.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r5.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p578#2/r5.claim: A report from Abu al-Darda says nothing is delayed once its appointed term comes; righteous descendants' prayers can benefit a person in the grave and thereby increase his lifespan.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r6.claim: If God punished people immediately for their wrongdoing, no creature would remain: creatures are either culpable or depend on human life, as in the time of Noah.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r7.claim: Here ẓulm includes actual and latent shirk; the reciprocal form of “take to account” conveys especially thorough reckoning.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r8.claim: The phrase “on it” covers every creature on earth or within it, making this formulation broader than the wording in Sūrat Fāṭir.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p280/r9.claim: God delays people mercifully and wisely until a term fixed from eternity; once it arrives, they cannot delay or advance it by even an hour.

DURR-FULL:v5p139/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r10.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r10.claim: Anas says a lizard nearly died in its burrow from fear of human wrongdoing.

DURR-FULL:v5p139/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r11.speaker: أبو هريرة
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r11.claim: Abu Hurayra answers that injustice harms others too: the bustard may die thin and distressed because of a wrongdoer's injustice.

DURR-FULL:v5p139/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r6.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr says that if God seized people for wrongdoing, He would withhold rain from them.

DURR-FULL:v5p139/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r7.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r7.claim: Al-Suddi says drought would kill every animal on earth if rain stopped.

DURR-FULL:v5p139/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r8.claim: Qatadah says God did this in Noah's time, destroying all creatures on earth except those carried in Noah's ark.

DURR-FULL:v5p139/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v5p139/r9.claim: Ibn Masud says human sins have killed or nearly punished small creatures in their burrows; he cites a reading that says on its back rather than on it.

BURSEVI:v5p34#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p34#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p34#2/r1.claim: God delays people with forbearance until a fixed term, whether their lifetimes or punishment, allowing them to multiply or their punishment to increase; when it arrives, they cannot postpone it.

BURSEVI:v5p34#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p34#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p34#2/r2.claim: The form of ‘seek to delay’ highlights their inability even if they want it; an hour is the briefest interval, and inability to advance emphasizes the impossibility of changing the term.

BURSEVI:v5p34/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p34/r1.speaker: الحجاج
BURSEVI:v5p34/r1.claim: Asked about the most pleasing sound, one courtier names Quran recitation at night, another news of a newborn son, and Shuʿba ibn ʿAlqama hearing food served when hungry; al-Hajjaj jokes that Tamim people insist on food.

BURSEVI:v5p34/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p34/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p34/r2.claim: Were people punished for wrongdoing, every creature on earth would perish; animals die at their appointed terms, whereas human destruction is punishment for injustice.

BURSEVI:v5p34/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p34/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
BURSEVI:v5p34/r3.claim: Abu Hurayra rejects the claim that an oppressor harms only himself: even a bustard dies in its nest because of the oppressor’s wrongdoing.

BURSEVI:v5p34/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p34/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
BURSEVI:v5p34/r4.claim: Ibn Masʿud says universal punishment for human sins would reach every creature, even beetles in their holes, and stop rain; God instead delays through forgiveness and grace.

BURSEVI:v5p34/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p34/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p34/r5.claim: Wrongdoing harms outwardly and inwardly: burning one house can spread across a neighborhood or city and kill animals and insects.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r1.claim: The threatened people are either wrongdoers in general or, according to a narrower view, only disbelievers; مؤاخذة is a reciprocal form used in the sense of taking to account.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r2.claim: Ibn Atiyya figuratively explains taking to account as the servant seizing God's due by sin and God taking it back through punishment.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r3.claim: Wrongdoing here means sins because they are improper acts placed outside their proper order, though it may be restricted to disbelief and aggression.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r4.claim: The hypothetical destruction clarifies God's might and wisdom and signals that the disbelievers' wrongdoing has reached an extreme.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r5.claim: The earth is understood from the mention of people and the familiar idea of creatures moving on it; all animals would be destroyed, the wrongdoers for their sins and others by their misfortune.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra counters a man's claim that injustice harms only the unjust: even a bustard in its nest dies of starvation because of a wrongdoer's injustice.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v14p170#2/r7.claim: Ibn Masʿud says Adam's descendants' sins nearly caused a dung beetle to perish in its burrow; he links this to Noah's flood.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r1.claim: The first argument from the verse is that its hypothetical wording entails that God did not punish people for their wrongdoing and left at least one creature alive.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r2.claim: The second argument is that universal punishment would leave no creature, yet many animals remain; therefore God did not exact such punishment.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r3.claim: The alternative claim that harms are lawful without being retribution is rejected by consensus, supporting a default prohibition of harms.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r4.claim: If a specific text permits a harmful act, it takes precedence over the general rule; without such evidence, the act remains forbidden.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r5.speaker: المعتزلة
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r5.claim: The Muʿtazilites use the verse to argue that human beings create their own acts; al-Alusi says the argument and response are obvious.

ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v14p171/r6.claim: God delays people to an appointed term—perhaps for reproduction or to increase their punishment—and no one can gain or lose even an hour from it.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r1.claim: Because wrongdoing and association with God were widespread, immediate destruction of every wrongdoer would eventually empty the whole earth of people and animals, including by the time of revelation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r2.claim: God can miraculously rescue righteous people from such destruction, as in Q 39:61 and the deliverances of Hūd and Noah.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r3.claim: The appointed term varies across peoples; staggered deadlines let many communities continue to inhabit the earth.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r4.claim: “Every animal” includes the animals of the destroyed people, since livestock were made for human benefit and can be destroyed with their owners.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r5.claim: Mentioning animals concisely also entails the destruction of the oppressors themselves, by implication.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r6.claim: This is total eradication, unlike ordinary disasters and social trials, which follow natural causes and may strike bystanders; sparing the righteous in those events preserves the natural order and its benefits, as in Q 8:25.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p189/r7.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports the Prophet saying that when God intends punishment for a people, it strikes those present and they are resurrected according to their intentions; a righteous person is rewarded for the collateral calamity, while the innocent do not receive the afterlife penalty, as in Q 6:164.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r1.claim: Animals on earth are made for human benefit, so using them for their intended purposes or slaughtering them for food is not injustice to them.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r2.claim: مؤاخذة is taking someone to requite them; its intensive form conveys severity, and the negated taking is prompt punishment, which ordinarily follows wrongdoing.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r3.claim: The “but He postpones them” clause corrects the expectation of immediate retribution, and أجل مسمى means a specified, fixed term.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v14p190/r4.claim: A similar statement that no community can delay or advance its term occurs in Q 7:34.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p414/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p414/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p414/r6.claim: God's gentleness prevents hardship from being unrelieved, as reflected in the statement that if God punished people for wrongdoing He would leave no creature alive.

TABATABAI:16:41-64#3/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:41-64#3/r7.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TABATABAI:16:41-64#3/r7.claim: A report from Abū Hurayra says that if God punished the Prophet and Jesus for their sins, or for what their two hands had done, He would punish them without injustice.

TABATABAI:16:41-64#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:41-64#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:41-64#4/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says the Abū Hurayra report conflicts with the Qurʾān and Sunna on prophetic infallibility; it cannot mean punishment for merely leaving the preferable, since that incurs no punishment.

TABATABAI:16:61/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r1.claim: The reading that animals exist for people’s use is supported by the statement that God created everything on earth for you.

TABATABAI:16:61/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r10.claim: The author rejects the rain-withholding explanation because the wording gives no evidence for it.

TABATABAI:16:61/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r11.claim: The delay clause supplies the omitted sense that God does not punish immediately; an appointed term means an individual’s death, a nation’s extinction, or the end of humankind at the Trumpet.

TABATABAI:16:61/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r2.claim: On the human-only reading, continued punishment would leave no moving human: most would perish for their wrongdoing, while the rare infallible prophets and Imams would never be born because their parents and ancestors had already perished.

TABATABAI:16:61/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r3.claim: Other answers defending the general reading of creature as all animals and humans are not reproduced because the author sees no benefit in listing them.

TABATABAI:16:61/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r4.claim: The verse does not prove that every person who perishes is personally sinful or that prophets lack immunity: it predicts universal extinction under immediate punishment, while some could perish through their ancestors’ deaths.

TABATABAI:16:61/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r5.claim: One proposed defense limits people to wrongdoers because the verse says for their wrongdoing, excluding the infallible from the outset.

TABATABAI:16:61/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r6.claim: The author rejects limiting people to wrongdoers: then only wrongdoers would die, leaving no reason for the verse to say that all creatures on earth would perish.

TABATABAI:16:61/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r7.claim: Another response broadens wrongdoing to include leaving the preferable, a breach of an indicative rather than binding command that may occur from prophets, as in Adam’s prayer.

TABATABAI:16:61/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r8.claim: He rejects that broadening because the context concerns shirk and violations of binding commands, and the promised appointed term has the tone of threat rather than a reference to leaving the preferable.

TABATABAI:16:61/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:16:61/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:16:61/r9.claim: A third answer says God may withhold rain because of human wrongdoing, destroying animals and righteous people too; for them the calamity is a trial and greater reward.

ASAD-NOTES:16:61#n68/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:61#n68/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:61#n68/r1.claim: The appointed term may be one known only to God; the respite gives people time to reflect and repent during earthly life.

ASAD-NOTES:16:61#n69/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:16:61#n69/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:16:61#n69/r1.claim: Asad renders sa'ah as a single moment, as in his note on 7:34.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: God gives respite because each event has an appointed time; when it arrives, it cannot be delayed or advanced.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet is assured that earlier messengers faced the same opposition; his duty is to convey the truth conclusively, not convert people.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r1.claim: The ‘wrongdoing’ here means the Meccan polytheists’ false beliefs and abuses, especially attacks on Islam and Muslims; associating partners with God is its root, and shirk is called a great wrong (31:13).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r2.claim: Although Meccan pagans are the immediate target, all humanity is addressed because they are neither the first nor last to fall into shirk, disbelief, evil, and injustice; the Qur’an aims to educate humanity in true belief and good conduct.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r3.claim: God does not immediately punish even disbelievers and wrongdoers, but gives them a fixed term through justice, mercy, and generosity; this patience offers time to reform, while communities persisting in error eventually disappear.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r4.speaker: some commentators
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r4.claim: Because dabba often means creatures other than humans, commentators have discussed how people’s sins could harm other creatures (Razi, 20:59–60).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:16:61/r5.claim: The author takes dabba figuratively: this warning concerns people, not animals without religious responsibility, though human wrongdoing in fact harms other creatures too.

STUDYQURAN:16:61/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r1.claim: This verse is compared with 35:45 and 18:58.

STUDYQURAN:16:61/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r2.claim: Rather than punish people immediately, God grants them reprieve until an appointed term.

STUDYQURAN:16:61/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r3.claim: This reprieve applies only during life; God gives no soul more time once its term arrives.

STUDYQURAN:16:61/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r4.claim: God gives respite to Satan and to human wrongdoers in several states.

STUDYQURAN:16:61/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r5.claim: Respite may allow repentance, but it can also let wrongdoers increase in sin or let Satan cause others to sin.

STUDYQURAN:16:61/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r6.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r6.claim: A respite does not prove permanent safety from punishment or divine approval.

STUDYQURAN:16:61/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:61/r7.claim: Other verses also say people cannot advance or delay their appointed term.

STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:16:intro/r16.claim: The surah repeatedly warns disbelievers of punishment in this world and the Hereafter.
